classification.difficultyReason: Rationalise four binomial denominators and recognise cancellation across the resulting sum.

answer.short:
$1$

Rationalise each denominator using its conjugate; the intermediate surd terms cancel.
answer.worked:
Multiply each numerator and denominator by the conjugate of its denominator:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{1}{1+\sqrt3}&=\frac{\sqrt3-1}{3-1}=\frac{\sqrt3-1}{2}\\\frac{1}{\sqrt3+\sqrt5}&=\frac{\sqrt5-\sqrt3}{5-3}=\frac{\sqrt5-\sqrt3}{2}\\\frac{1}{\sqrt5+\sqrt7}&=\frac{\sqrt7-\sqrt5}{7-5}=\frac{\sqrt7-\sqrt5}{2}\\\frac{1}{\sqrt7+3}&=\frac{3-\sqrt7}{9-7}=\frac{3-\sqrt7}{2}\end{align*}$$
Adding gives
$$\begin{align*}\frac{1}{1+\sqrt3}+\frac{1}{\sqrt3+\sqrt5}+\frac{1}{\sqrt5+\sqrt7}+\frac{1}{\sqrt7+3}&=\frac{\sqrt3-1+\sqrt5-\sqrt3+\sqrt7-\sqrt5+3-\sqrt7}{2}\\\frac{1}{1+\sqrt3}+\frac{1}{\sqrt3+\sqrt5}+\frac{1}{\sqrt5+\sqrt7}+\frac{1}{\sqrt7+3}&=\frac{3-1}{2}\\\frac{1}{1+\sqrt3}+\frac{1}{\sqrt3+\sqrt5}+\frac{1}{\sqrt5+\sqrt7}+\frac{1}{\sqrt7+3}&=1\end{align*}$$
